> **Decomposed 2026-09-01 into three children (below), all downstream of #255.** This body is now the
> brief for the root's own attempt — the verify-and-synthesize pass after every child has closed. The
> original design is preserved under *Design record* at the bottom: it is what each child was given.

## Why

Three PRs built the tool posture, each reviewed on its own. Nobody has checked that the pieces fit, and no child
could write the documentation describing the whole.

## What

You are the root of a track. Your blockers' results arrive under **Parent task results**, but only for
the leaves you are directly blocked by — so read the others yourself before you start:

```
hkb show 256
hkb show 257
hkb show 258
hkb show 255   # the shared seam both this track and its sibling track depend on
```

**Do not redo their work.** Your job is the seam and the story:

1. **Run it for real** against this board and say what you saw.
2. **Check the pieces agree**: the exported vocabulary against what the docs and the brief claim, and
   every derived grant against `effectiveTools` (#255) rather than a second computation.
3. **Check the promise that nothing changes for a board that declares nothing** still holds end to end —
   it is asserted per child, and the whole is where it actually has to be true.
4. **Write what no child could**: the wiki page for the feature as one thing, and a `docs/wiki/log.md` entry.
5. **Report the gaps you did not fix** in your summary, as cards to file rather than silent edits.

## Done when

- [ ] The feature runs end to end on this board, described in the summary from what you actually saw.
- [ ] Every derived grant goes through `effectiveTools`; nothing computes a second answer.
- [ ] A board declaring nothing is byte-identically unchanged, verified across all three children.
- [ ] One wiki page describes the feature as a whole; `wiki-check.mjs` is clean for it.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test && npm run smoke` pass.

---

# Design record

*The original card, unchanged. The children above are how it was cut.*

> Filed 2026-09-01 from the operator's framing: "if I run hkb on my machine and in a repo I usually want workers
> to inherit my skills, tools and mcp... then there is a case where people would like to curate what power a
> worker has — say a worker has access to a supabase mcp that writes to production, they might not want to leave
> an unattended worker using it."

## Why

hkb has one posture and it is hardcoded. `CLAUDE_TOOLS` (`src/board.js`) is a fixed allowlist — shell patterns
plus `Edit, Write, Read, Glob, Grep, Skill` — and workers launch `--permission-mode dontAsk`, which **denies** an
unlisted tool rather than prompting. The launch line passes no MCP configuration at all, so a worker inherits
whatever `.mcp.json` the repo has and is then refused every tool those servers expose.

Nobody chose that posture per board; it is what the default happens to be. And it is the *curated* end of the
range, silently, on every board hkb has ever initialised.

The cost is measured, on this board, in #130: **208 native denials across 56 of 71 attempts, and not one of them
ended the attempt.** Every worker routed around silently. The example that should decide this card: piloting on
`french-tech-homies/pipao-v2`, a worker denied the `react-aria` MCP server *sitting in the repo's own
`.mcp.json`* built the components from training knowledge and said nothing. The output looked fine.

So the two failures are symmetrical and both are live:

- **Too narrow, silently** — the worker cannot reach the thing the repo installed for exactly this job, does not
  say so, and produces a worse answer that reads like a good one.
- **Too wide, dangerously** — an unattended worker reaches a tool whose blast radius is production. Nothing in
  hkb today lets a board say "these tools, and not that one", except by hand-editing one flat list.

There is no layer between them, and no per-card adjustment at all: `allowed_tools` is per-profile, `kb.skills` is
per-card but only names skills (#114), and neither knows about MCP servers.

## What

- **An explicit posture on the profile**, so the choice is made rather than inherited:
  - `"tools": "inherit"` — the session's own environment: the human's skills, the repo's MCP servers, the
    harness's default tool policy. What somebody running hkb in their own repo on their own machine expects.
  - `"tools": "curate"` — today's behaviour: an explicit allowlist, everything else denied. The right default
    for a shared board, CI, or any launch nobody is watching.
  The board declares which; `hkb init` should ask or default conservatively and *say which it chose*, because a
  posture nobody knows about is the current bug.
- **MCP servers are named, not implied.** Under `curate`, a profile lists the servers a worker may reach
  (`"mcp": ["react-aria"]`); under `inherit`, it may list servers to *exclude*. The supabase-writes-to-production
  case has to be expressible as a subtraction, not only as a whitelist nobody remembers to maintain.
- **A card narrows, never widens.** `kb.tools` / `kb.mcp` on a task can only be a subset of what the profile
  grants. A card that could grant itself a capability is the seat problem one rung down: the board is the
  ceiling, a card lowers it, and nothing raises it but a human editing `.kanban/board.json`. Enforce it in a pure
  `effectiveTools(profile, task)` in `src/model.js`, and make the "widening is ignored, here is what was
  dropped" case a test, not a comment.
- **The ledger is what makes the dial turnable.** #130 records what a worker was refused; this card is what a
  human does about it. They only work together — a posture with no feedback is a guess, and a ledger with no
  dial is a complaint. #130 should also record what was **used**, not only what was denied: "which grant is
  nobody using" is as much a decision input as "which denial keeps happening", and only the denial half is
  currently specified.
- **`hkb doctor`** prints each profile's posture, its MCP list, and whether any open card asks for something its
  profile does not grant.

**Relationship to the neighbours** — worth settling before building, not this card's call: #217 (capability map)
binds an *intent* to a harness command; this card decides *how much power* a worker has. They meet at
`allowed_tools`, and if both land, the grant should be derived from the union of the map and the posture rather
than maintained twice — which is #217's whole argument, applied here.

## Done when

- [ ] A profile declares `inherit` or `curate`; `hkb init` picks one, says which, and writes it down.
- [ ] Under `curate`, a worker reaches only the named tools and MCP servers; under `inherit`, it reaches the
      session's own environment minus any exclusions.
- [ ] `kb.tools` / `kb.mcp` on a card can only narrow; an attempt to widen is dropped, recorded, and covered by
      a test in `src/model.js`.
- [ ] `hkb doctor` prints the posture and flags a card asking for what its profile does not grant.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; a wiki page states the ceiling rule in one sentence.
goal: A profile declares inherit or curate and init says which; curate names its tools and MCP servers and inherit can exclude; a card can only narrow what its profile grants, with widening dropped and tested; doctor prints the posture and flags a card asking for what it cannot have
title: A profile has one hardcoded tool posture nobody chose, so workers are silently denied the repo's own MCP servers and a board cannot say which power an unattended worker may hold
